hook: Replacement architecture. The detox fails without this.
topic: Building a replacement plan for reclaimed time
body:
**Replacement architecture. The detox fails without it. Most people skip it.**

When you remove high-stimulus inputs, you create time. Unstructured time that your brain will immediately attempt to fill with the highest-available-reward option. If you haven't pre-decided what fills it, the default behaviour returns within 48 hours. Not because you lack discipline — because a vacuum always gets filled.

The replacement has to be pre-loaded, low-friction, and low-to-medium stimulus. Not a new high-intensity habit — that just substitutes one calibration problem for another. The goal is an activity that occupies the time, builds slowly, and doesn't re-spike the threshold.

Practical options that work within the framework: long-form reading, physical output, a specific project, structured walking, single-skill practice. The specificity matters. "I'll read more" is not architecture. "I'll read from 8:30 to 9:30 with the phone in another room" is architecture.

The replacement plan needs to be written before you start the reset. On paper. With time slots. If it's not specific enough to be a schedule, it's not specific enough to work.

Template is in the link in bio.
